\begin{theorem}[Endpoint convergence]\label{m:main}
For every fixed integer $n\geq3$ and every complex-valued
$f\in H^{s_n}(\R^n)$, there is a full-measure set $E_f$ of Lebesgue
points of $f$ and a function $v(x,t)$, $x\in E_f$, $0\leq t<1$, such
that $v(x,\cdot)$ is continuous, $v(x,0)=f^*(x)$, and
\begin{equation}\label{m:eq-uniform-Gaussian}
 \lim_{a\downarrow0}\sup_{0<t<1}|U_af(x,t)-v(x,t)|=0
 \qquad(x\in E_f).
\end{equation}
In particular the finite Gaussian limit
\[
 u_f(x,t)=\lim_{a\downarrow0}U_af(x,t)
\]
exists for every real $0<t<1$ on this one set, and
$\lim_{t\downarrow0}u_f(x,t)=f^*(x)$.
\end{theorem}

The Gaussian limit is taken first.  No Fourier support, radiality,
logarithmic strengthening of $H^{s_n}$, or additional regularity is
assumed.  The theorem concerns all real times approaching zero, not a
chosen sequence.

Sj\"olin and Vega independently obtained convergence for $s>1/2$
in higher dimensions \citep{Sjolin1987,Vega1988}.  At $s>1/2$,

\begin{lemma}[Exact-centering comparison]\label{lem:center-transfer}
Let the true and pasted dynamics start from the same initial ensemble.
Under the cutoff estimate of \Cref{prop:cutoff}, the expectation of
any fixed bounded empirical observation list differs between the two
dynamics by \(o(\mu^{-1/2})\).  Consequently the corresponding
exact-centered fluctuation vectors have the same weak limits.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\mathcal E_\eps\) be the event that the two trajectories separate
at some time in \([0,T]\).  By \Cref{prop:cutoff},
\(\P(\mathcal E_\eps)=O(\eps^{1+\eta})\) for some \(\eta>0\).
Both dynamics preserve \(N\), and their observations coincide on its
complement.  For the scalar record sum, denoted by \(S^{\eps,\mathrm{tr}}\)
and \(S^\eps\) on the two dynamics,
\[
 |S^{\eps,\mathrm{tr}}-S^\eps|
       \le 2M_{\mathrm{obs}}N\ind_{\mathcal E_\eps}.
\]
Choose an integer \(p>(1+\eta)/\eta\).  By Hölder's inequality and
\eqref{eq:initial-N-moments},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:limit-center-estimate}
 \begin{split}
 \frac{|\E S^{\eps,\mathrm{tr}}-\E S^\eps|}{\sqrt\mu}
 &\le 2M_{\mathrm{obs}}\sqrt\mu
       \bigl(\E(N/\mu)^p\bigr)^{1/p}
            \P(\mathcal E_\eps)^{1-1/p}\\
 &\le C_p\,\eps^{-1+(1+\eta)(1-1/p)}
       \longrightarrow0.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
There is a nonnegative density \(F_0\) on \(\T^3\times\R^3\), with bounded
velocity support and
\[
\int_{\T^3\times\R^3}
 F_0(1+|v|^2+|\log F_0|)\dd x\dd v<\infty,
\]
for which the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation has two distinct global
admissible solutions, in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:admissible},
with initial datum \(F_0\).
On some common initial interval both solutions are strongly continuous
in \(L^1\), and their collision gains and losses are integrable in
space-time-velocity.
\end{theorem}

The two solutions therefore obey the unrenormalized equation on the
interval where their difference is established. Their common datum has
bounded velocities but unbounded amplitudes concentrated at successively
smaller spatial scales. The conservation and dissipation requirements
remain part of the conclusion.

\subsection{Uniqueness and related constructions}

Classical uniqueness theorems impose additional control, such as
Maxwellian upper bounds \cite{KanielShinbrot1978}. For periodic cutoff
hard potentials, Ukai's perturbative theory gives global existence and
uniqueness near a Maxwellian in a velocity-weighted spatial Sobolev class,
with mass, momentum, and energy matched to that Maxwellian
\cite[Theorem~1.2]{Ukai1974}.

\begin{definition}[Entropy solution with local conservation]
\label{def:admissible}
Let \(F_0\ge0\) have finite mass, energy, and absolute entropy.
A global entropy solution with local conservation is a nonnegative
function \(F\) satisfying the following conditions.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \(F\in C_w([0,\infty);L^1(\Omega))\), \(F(0)=F_0\), with
continuity against every bounded measurable test. For every finite \(T\),
\[
 \sup_{0\le t\le T}\int_\Omega
 F(t)(1+|v|^2+|\log F(t)|)\dd x\dd v<\infty.
\]
\item The two functions \(Q^\pm(F,F)/(1+G)\) belong to
\(L^1([0,T]\times\Omega)\) for every finite \(T\).
For every \(\beta\in C^1([0,\infty))\) with \(\beta(0)=0\) and
\(|\beta'(z)|\le C_\beta/(1+z)\), and every smooth \(\varphi\) periodic
in \(x\) and compactly supported in \([0,\infty)\times\R^3_v\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:renormalized}
\begin{split}
 &\int_0^\infty\!\!\int_\Omega
 \left[M\beta(G)\D\varphi+\beta'(G)Q(F,F)\varphi\right]
                  \dd x\dd v\dd t\\
 &\hspace{15mm}
 +\int_\Omega M\beta(F_0/M)\varphi(0,x,v)\dd x\dd v=0.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
\item Total momentum is conserved. At every \(t\ge0\),
\[
 \int_\Omega |v|^2F(t)\dd x\dd v\le\int_\Omega |v|^2F_0\dd x\dd v,
 \qquad
 \mathcal H_M(F(t))+\int_0^t\mathcal D(F(s))\dd s
      \le\mathcal H_M(F_0).

There exist \(R<\infty\) and a nonnegative datum \(F_0\) with

The starting point is the concentrating-jet mechanism of

entropy class. Its continuation theorem does not supply the exact local

are reproduced below with attribution; the new estimates concern the

\subsection{History and scope}

The Boltzmann--Grad scaling goes back to Grad~\cite{Grad49,Grad58}.
Lanford established the hard-sphere limit on a short time
interval~\cite{Lanford75}, and King's thesis treated positive
finite-range potentials~\cite{King75}.
Gallagher, Saint-Raymond, and Texier gave a detailed geometric analysis
of recollisions for hard spheres and a class of repulsive potentials,
including a convergence rate in the hard-sphere case~\cite{GST14}.
Pulvirenti, Saffirio, and Simonella proved a short-time theorem for the
stable radial class used here; see their Section~8, Hypothesis~1$'$ and
Theorem~1$'$~\cite{PSS14}. Their treatment permits attractive parts and
does not require a globally single-valued differential cross-section.

\[
 P=(1/4,1/4,0),\qquad
 \mathcal O=\{(X,Y,Z)\in\mathbb T^3:1/32<Y<1/8\},
\]
the material trajectory from $P$ enters $\mathcal O$ at a finite
time if and only if the machine halts on the input.
\end{enumerate}
The force is specified by a finite formula which does not simulate the
chosen execution.  The construction is also uniform as a formula in
an arbitrary positive parameter $\nu$.
\end{theorem}
For a fixed positive noncomputable $\nu$, the same finite formulas and
mathematical conclusions hold, with evaluation relative to that
parameter. The algorithmic assertion concerns computable $\nu$.
The force can also be made solenoidal by the periodic
Helmholtz--Leray projection; this changes the pressure, not the velocity.
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} concerns these explicitly supplied smooth
solutions and is not a regularity theorem for arbitrary fluid data.
